facts.claim: For a field with formControl and no fieldGroup, the field subscription uses debounce.default only when it is positive and updateOn is absent or change. In that branch it subscribes to control.valueChanges.pipe(debounceTime(debounce.default)), delaying the Formly model-assignment and fieldChanges emission path.

limits: This is Formly propagation timing, not a debounce implementation for Angular validation or application HTTP requests; blur and submit do not take this branch.

facts.claim: In the ordinary non-debounced leaf-control subscription, Formly passes each emitted value through field.parsers in array order, feeding each result to the next parser. If the final result is not Object.is-equal to the control value, it writes the parsed result back with formControl.setValue(value).
facts.context: parsers normalization writeback raw text idempotent
limits: Write-back can emit again; normalization should stabilize. Parsers are not a separate raw-view/normalized-model store, and this source does not qualify a custom value accessor or browser display.

facts.claim: A positive debounce.default with absent/change updateOn replaces the parser/distinctUntilChanged pipeline, including any conditional startWith(control.value) added for an initial model/control mismatch, with raw control.valueChanges.pipe(debounceTime(...)). This branch bypasses those parser, deduplication and initial-value-start operators in the field subscription.

limits: This is a pinned 6.3.12 source limitation, not an endorsement of mixing Formly debounce with required normalization or a claim about another release.

facts.claim: The leaf-control subscription assigns the emitted value through assignFieldValue when the field has a key, then emits options.fieldChanges with { value, field, type: valueChanges }. Keyless leaf controls still emit the field event without that keyed model assignment.
facts.context: control.valueChanges fieldChanges model assignment event order keyless
limits: An arbitrary external control.valueChanges subscriber is not a completed root-model transaction boundary. This leaf path does not describe every array or expression event producer.
